title: Celsius Symbol: Copy & Paste ℃ Degree Celsius Sign
meta_description: Copy and paste the degree Celsius sign (℃, U+2103) — the single-character temperature ligature, why Unicode recommends plain °C instead, and how to type it on Windows and Mac. Click any symbol to copy it.
hero_tagline: ℃ is a single Unicode character that packs the degree sign and a capital C into one glyph — handy to paste, though most typographers still reach for plain °C. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: The degree Celsius sign (℃, Unicode U+2103) is a precomposed character in the Letterlike Symbols block that combines the degree sign (°) and a capital C into a single glyph. It exists mainly so that older East Asian text — where a full temperature reading often occupied one character cell — could round-trip through Unicode without changing length. For new text, Unicode and most style guides actually recommend writing the degree sign followed by a plain C (°C) rather than the one-character ℃, but the single glyph remains the fastest thing to copy when you just need the mark.
